Position scales for the value axis of a pyramid

Source: R/scale-pyramid.R
scale_x_pyramid.Rd

scale_x_pyramid() and scale_y_pyramid() are continuous position scales that label the value axis of a pyramid without the minus sign and extend it equally far on both sides of zero. coord_pyramid() does the same for a horizontal pyramid, along with placing the age axis; these scales serve a vertical pyramid, or a plot that needs another coordinate system.

Usage

scale_x_pyramid(..., labels = waiver(), limits = NULL, symmetric = TRUE)

scale_y_pyramid(..., labels = waiver(), limits = NULL, symmetric = TRUE)

Arguments

...

Other arguments passed on to ggplot2::scale_x_continuous() or ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(), such as breaks, expand or position.

labels

Labels for the breaks, applied to their absolute values. One of:

  • a function that takes the breaks and returns labels, such as scales::label_comma(), or a formula such as ~ .x / 1000;

  • the default, waiver(), for the usual number format;

  • a character vector of labels, used as given;

  • NULL for no labels.

limits

One of:

  • NULL to use the default scale range

  • A numeric vector of length two providing limits of the scale. Use NA to refer to the existing minimum or maximum

  • A function that accepts the existing (automatic) limits and returns new limits. Also accepts rlang lambda function notation. Note that setting limits on positional scales will remove data outside of the limits. If the purpose is to zoom, use the limit argument in the coordinate system (see coord_cartesian()).

symmetric

If TRUE, the limits extend equally far on both sides of zero. Ignored when limits is set.

Value

A ggplot2 scale.

See also

coord_pyramid(), which labels and limits the value axis of a horizontal pyramid.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

france <- subset(europe_pop, country == "France" & year == 2024)

# A vertical pyramid, with age on x
ggplot(france, aes(x = age, y = population, fill = sex)) +
  geom_pyramid() +
  scale_y_pyramid(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5))
